Definition: from G5561; to be in (give) space, i.e. (intransitively) to pass, enter, or (transitively) to hold, admit (literally or figuratively):--come, contain, go, have place, (can, be room to) receive.
BiblicalUsage: Choreo is to make room, to contain or to receive, and the New Testament uses it for hearts, for vessels and for repentance. Paul asks the Corinthians to receive him, the waterpots at Cana contain two or three firkins apiece, the crowds press so that there is no room to receive them, and Peter says God is not willing that any should perish but that all should come to repentance.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe making room is the heart of the gospel, because God makes room for sinners and asks us to make room for one another. I hold that the room God makes for repentance is the widest room of all, and it is still open.
